title: ACA s. 29 — Decision making by panel of arbitrators

content.overview: Section 29 governs decision-making where the arbitral tribunal has more than one arbitrator. Unless the parties agree otherwise, decisions are by majority of all tribunal members; questions of procedure may be decided by the presiding arbitrator only where authorised by the parties or all tribunal members.
content.glance: Section 29 governs decision-making where the arbitral tribunal has more than one arbitrator. Unless the parties agree otherwise, decisions are by majority of all tribunal members; questions of procedure may be decided by the presiding arbitrator only where authorised by the parties or all tribunal members.
content.study:
Module 1: Majority rule
Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, a multi-member tribunal decides by majority of all its members.

Module 2: Procedural questions
The presiding arbitrator may decide questions of procedure only when authorised by the parties or all members of the tribunal.

Module 3: Limits of presiding arbitrator's role
The special statutory authority for procedural questions should not be converted into a general unilateral power to decide the merits.

provisions.title: Decision making by panel of arbitrators

examples.title: Rule applies
examples.body: A three-member tribunal votes on the merits and two members form the majority; the statutory majority rule applies absent a contrary party agreement.

examples.title: Rule fails or changes
examples.body: The presiding arbitrator decides a merits question alone merely because the tribunal had authorised unilateral handling of procedural matters; section 29(2) does not supply that merits authority.

hypotheticals.question: Does section 29(2) permit the presiding arbitrator to decide the merits alone?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Its special authority concerns questions of procedure and depends on the specified authorisation.

distinctions.title: Majority decision and procedural decision
distinctions.rows: Presiding arbitrator may decide procedural questions only with the required authorisation.

misconceptions.trap: Reading the presiding arbitrator's procedural power as a general merits power.
misconceptions.correction: Separate merits decision-making from the narrowly conditioned procedural authority in section 29(2).

questionsAndAnswers.question: How are decisions made by a multi-member tribunal?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: By majority of all members unless the parties have agreed otherwise; procedural questions may be decided by the presiding arbitrator when properly authorised.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: Always identify the nature of the question before invoking section 29(2).

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should section 29 be applied in submissions?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Start with the statutory text, identify every condition and then apply the facts to the precise statutory consequence.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: Keep the submission statute-led and distinguish discretion, conditions and consequence.
